title: Choose Kumo's visual world
question: The roll assigned The Bestiary Sheet. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll. The current mint-to-violet gradient is the category rut and is out either way.

options.label: The Bestiary Sheet
options.lineage: Tabletop bestiary spreads and character sheets
options.thesis: Your creature is a specimen entry, and your habits are the stat block that made it.
options.viewport: The creature sits centred on a ruled plate, its lineage named beneath like a binomial, with mind/body/order scored in the margin.
options.risk: Goes musty if the rules get thin and the ground goes cream instead of ink.

options.label: Provenance Ribbon
options.thesis: A habit history is a custody line: unbroken stretches, honest gaps, and returns.
options.case: Fuses well: a missed day becomes unwoven thread instead of a red cross, which suits the no-punishment rule. Weaker on the creature itself, which is the thing people come back for.

options.label: Gravity Rain Garden
options.thesis: Each habit is a cloud with its own gravity, and the glade is what the rain built.
options.case: The glade would be gorgeous and the art would sit in it beautifully. Fuses poorly with the daily job: it wants exploring, and the real visit is a three-second tap.

options.label: Darkroom Safelight
options.thesis: The creature develops in the tray, appearing slowly as the days accumulate.
options.case: The amber ground is a genuinely fresh answer for a night-time app. Fuses poorly on principle: its whole drama is that pulling the print too early loses it, and this product refuses to punish.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: The habit-app look every competitor ships, executed impeccably.
canonCard.viewport: Soft rounded cards, a friendly accent, generous white space, done properly rather than approximately.
